memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension loader, agent-system/extensions/*/context/ trees deploy into ONE shared merged .claude/context/ directory, not per-extension namespaced trees (.claude/extensions/<ext>/ holds only manifest.json). When two extensions' index-entries.json declare the same relative path (e.g. core and lean both declare contracts/adversarial-verification.md), merge.lua's append_index_entries does an upsert-by-path: whichever extension is processed LAST for a given load/sync run fully replaces both the file content and the index entry (including load_when) at that path. This is a documented 'dormant' risk in merge.lua's own doc comment. Any new extension mirroring a core contract at the same relative path (e.g. cslib mirroring contracts/adversarial-verification.md) enters this same collision.

When an extension must mirror a core (or another extension's) index-entries.json contract entry that shares a deployed path, set load_when.agents to the UNION of every agent that should reach it, not just the mirroring extension's own agent. Because the loader's upsert-by-path fully replaces the whole entry object on a path match, a single-agent mirror silently drops every other agent's hook whenever the mirroring extension is processed last. Verified concretely: applying core's entry (agents=[general-research-hard-agent]) then a union-valued cslib entry (agents=[general-research-hard-agent, cslib-research-hard-agent]) via merge.append_index_entries yields one merged entry retaining both agent names.

To test neotex.plugins.ai.shared.extensions.merge's append_index_entries upsert behavior without performing a full extension deploy, run it directly via headless Neovim: package.path-extend to lua/, require the merge module, and call merge.append_index_entries(scratch_target, {entry}) repeatedly against a scratch JSON file, then inspect the result. This proves upsert-by-path outcomes (e.g. which fields survive a collision) without mutating .claude-extensions.json or the live deployed tree.
